objective_text: Plot complex numbers on complex plane

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 3 + 4i on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number 3 + 4i has a real part of 3 and an imaginary part of 4. In the complex plane, plot the point (3, 4).
questions.explanation: Remember that in the complex plane, the first number represents the real part and the second number represents the imaginary part.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to mix up the real and imaginary parts. Ensure the real part corresponds to the x-axis and the imaginary part to the y-axis.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number -2 - 5i on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number -2 - 5i has a real part of -2 and an imaginary part of -5. Plot the point (-2, -5) on the complex plane.
questions.explanation: When dealing with negative numbers, remember that a negative real part is to the left of the origin and a negative imaginary part is below the origin.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget about the sign changes for negative values. Plot negative real parts to the left and negative imaginary parts below.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 0 + 7i on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number 0 + 7i has a real part of 0 and an imaginary part of 7. Plot the point (0, 7) on the y-axis.
questions.explanation: When plotting a complex number with a zero real part, it lies exactly on the y-axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget that a zero real part places the point solely on the y-axis. Don't include an x-coordinate.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 6i on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number 6i has a real part of 0 and an imaginary part of 6. Plot the point (0, 6) on the y-axis.
questions.explanation: When plotting a pure imaginary number like 6i, remember that it lies exactly on the y-axis.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to include an x- coordinate when plotting a pure imaginary number. The real part is zero for these numbers.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number -4 + 0i on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number -4 + 0i has a real part of -4 and an imaginary part of 0. Plot the point (-4, 0) on the x-axis.
questions.explanation: When plotting a complex number with a zero imaginary part, it lies exactly on the x-axis. A negative real part places it to the left of the origin.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to forget about the sign change for the negative real part. Plot negative real parts to the left.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number 1 + i√3 on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number 1 + i√3 has a real part of 1 and an imaginary part of √3. Plot the point (1, √3) on the complex plane.
questions.explanation: When plotting complex numbers with non-integer values, use the exact values as given.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to approximate irrational or non-integer values. Plot them exactly as provided.

questions.stem: Plot the complex number -√2 + i√2 on the complex plane.
questions.solution: The complex number -√2 + i√2 has a real part of -√2 and an imaginary part of √2. Plot the point (-√2, √2) on the complex plane.
questions.explanation: When plotting complex numbers with non-integer values, use the exact values as given.
questions.common_mistake_notes: A common mistake is to approximate irrational or non-integer values. Plot them exactly as provided.
